description: Large square patio umbrella on a single centre pole with a valanced canvas canopy and a weighted base plate -- the one module in the outdoor roof set carried on one pole rather than four corner posts.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Large square patio umbrella on a single centre pole, canvas canopy stretched over eight radial ribs down to a short valanced edge, heavy round weighted base plate Materials: Cream canvas canopy with faint dirt streaking along the rib lines and mildew spotting at the seams, a sun-faded panel on one side, powder-coated aluminium pole chipped to bare metal at the base.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 1,280/4,000 triangles, 2/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 2/6 unique geometries, one 1024 px canvas at 5.6 MB, factory ~40 ms. check-coplanar clean; every azimuth turntable-gated with the closed canopy carrying the silhouette.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 4.000 x 3.300 x 4.000 m, nothing crossing the cell edge (tabs lean to 2.000 from a 1.985 canopy). The height was RE-DECLARED from the proxy (2.80 -> 3.30): the proxy's canopy rises 0.23 H over 0.535 H (23 degrees) and the build rises 0.80 over 2.0 (24) with a 0.30 valance to the 2.10 walk-under rim; base r 0.28 is the proxy's 0.205 H disc, the mast its 0.012 H stem.
featureReviews.notes: The first build was a 12-degree slab with a scalloped eave the plate does not have. The band-table residual is the declared 4 m width against the proxy's 1.07 W/H, recorded in the registry notes.

featureReviews.evidence: Canvas sagging 0.09 between eight ribs over seven rings (the sag reads on the 0 and 315 renders as soft valleys, where the first build's four rings were flat facets); a STRAIGHT valance with a pointed tab at each corner; a 0.68 m crown cap with a skirt over the vent and a round finial; eight ribs and eight struts from a runner collar under the canvas, seen from below.
featureReviews.notes: The plate shows one corner tab; the build gives every corner one. The cap reads slightly boxier than the plate's soft one.

featureReviews.evidence: One 1024 px dirt canvas mapped in PLAN: sixteen radial seam lines as four nested soft strokes with elongated smears, a warm cast on seven panels, 260 downhill dust streaks, crown grime, a valance strip with hem and top seams and drips. The canopy PROBED at luma 211-217 on the review render against the plate's 213-232 after carrying #dfd8cb as #d4cab8 for the harness's top-face lift.
featureReviews.notes: First pass drew the seams as 3 px lines with beaded clots and yellow wedges at alpha 0.4; widened, smeared and halved.

featureReviews.evidence: Cream painted pole (the plate's luma ~205, where the first build carried the base's #99978e) with a runner collar at 1.42 and a hub at 3.10, a bare steel spigot to 0.42 standing in a galvanised base disc with a raised boss.
featureReviews.notes: Paint chips and galvanising mottle are below the resolvable band on a 35 mm pole.

name: Square Patio Umbrella
nameTh: ร่มสนามสี่เหลี่ยม
notes: Part of a modular outdoor roof kit and sized to its grid: a 4 x 4 m canopy on the same 4 m module as the four-post bays, which divides the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles exactly 2 x 2. 4 m is a large commercial cafe umbrella rather than a domestic one, and it is deliberate -- the size is what lets this style be placed in a grid with the rest of the set instead of being a one-off. It is the one module in the set carried on a SINGLE CENTRE POLE, so it tiles differently from the four-post bays: placed side by side the canopies meet at their edges and leave the corners open, which is exactly how a real patio full of umbrellas covers ground, and it means the pole lands mid-bay rather than on the grid line. Canopy edge at about 2.1 m and peak at 2.8 m, so a player walks under the rim. Square rather than octagonal so that edges meet cleanly when several are placed together. The weighted base plate is part of the prop and sits on the ground: it is a trip hazard a player should collide with, not a detail to leave off. HEIGHT CORRECTED FROM THE PROXY BEFORE THE 2026-09-02 REBUILD: declared 4.00 x 2.80 (w/h 1.43), but the Meshy proxy of the plate measures the canopy at w/h 1.07 with the eave band at 0.66-0.77 H and the peak at 1.0 H -- a pyramid rising 0.23 H over a 0.535 H half-span (23 degrees), under which the built 2.10-edge / 2.80-peak canopy is a 12-degree slab. Width is the axis the grid fixes (4 m), and the walk-under edge stays at 2.10, so the height follows the pitch: valance 0.30 m to an eave at 2.40 and a peak at 3.30 gives 0.90 m of rise over the 2.0 m half-span, 24 degrees. The proxy at 4 m wide would be 3.74 m tall; 3.30 keeps the rim where a player walks under it and takes the plate's pitch. The remaining band-table residual (canopy 1.21 W/H against the proxy's 1.07) is that declaration.
